text:
Tony (ops): evening handoff — quick note before I sign off. saw a brief latency spike 18:12 UTC that touched embedding-read endpoints in eu-west. pages fired but auto-resolved after rotation to backup pool. leaving context for next shift and follow-ups.
incident-bot: paging: #pager-untriaged -> triggered at 1769999800 by embedding-read p95 > 1.2s. incidents: page-id=inc-20260315-99; severity=sev2; affected=eu-west embeddings; current_state=resolved->monitoring. link: https://incidents.redwood/inc-20260315-99
Priya (primary): thanks. I saw the same. root cause looks like a single pool hit with degraded NVMe perf during a background snapshot. embeddings autoscaler also briefly attempted to spin up, which increased tail queue.
Jordan (secondary): confirming — I pulled traces. KV cache hit-rate dropped around the same time (from 92% -> 71%) for the affected shard. suspect eviction storm from snapshot.
Tony (ops): action items already taken while I was watching: 1) rotated requests to backup pool using routing policy, 2) bumped cache TTL for embeddings for 10m as mitigation, 3) disabled autoscaler burst for that pool for now.
Maya (sre): logs snippet: ```
[18:11:58] embedding-read: p95=1300ms, inflight=120, queue_len=46
[18:12:06] pool-io: nvme_io_wait=230ms, snapshot=started
[18:12:18] routing: moved 60% traffic -> pool-b (backup)
[18:12:32] p95 back to 210ms, queue_len=5
```
Luis (eng): any deploys around that time? deploy-bot shows a non-prod snapshot job started at 18:10 on pool-a. not an app deploy, but disk snapshot which correlates.
deploy-bot: job(snapshot)-pool-a started 1769999400 by infra-snapshot-svc; duration=~9m; status=completed.
Priya (primary): customer impact: small. we saw a handful of user sessions with 5-8s response times before routing took effect. no error 5xx, just increased latency. estimated affected requests ~0.03% global, mostly EU developer integrations. flagged in customer-impact-triage.
Tony (ops): runbook pointer: follow runbook -> SRE Playbook Bot link for "storage-induced latency spike". quick checklist I used below.
SRE Playbook Bot: runbook: https://rwd.runbooks/storage-latency-spike v2.0. checklist: 
- verify pool IO metrics
- rotate routing to backup pool
- temporarily increase cache TTLs
- hold autoscaler/burst for affected pool
- open infra ticket if snapshot overlap expected

Maya (sre): next steps (short): 
- infra to verify snapshot scheduling configuration and avoid concurrency with peak traffic (assigned infra@)
- storage team to triage NVMe tail latency and setup alert for snapshot IO saturation
- oncall to monitor p95 for 60m, then remove temporary TTL bump if stable
- add a canary that prevents long-running snapshot jobs during 18:00-20:00 UTC if traffic crosses threshold

Jordan (secondary): I've added a follow-up ticket: TKT-embed-2026-042: investigate eviction pattern and autoscaler policy for pool-a. link: https://tickets.redwood/TKT-embed-2026-042
Priya (primary): coverage note: I'll be primary for the next 4 hours. Jordan will be secondary until 22:00 UTC. if escalation needed after that, ping oncall rotation (see rota).
Tony (ops): handoff checklist completed: 
- confirmed routing fallback worked
- mitigations applied (TTL, autoscaler hold)
- runbook link shared
- infra follow-up ticket created
- customer impact note in triage

Maya (sre): monitoring queries to keep an eye on (paste into grafana search): 
```
query: service:embedding-read.p95 by region
query: pool-a:nvme_io_wait.p99
query: cache:embedding:hit_rate by shard
```
Luis (eng): quick note for next shift: if you see nvme_io_wait rising with snapshot=running, don't restart agents on pool-a unless instructed — restarting can worsen queue. instead prefer routing and allow snapshot to finish.
Priya (primary): leaving this thread for the nightwatch. please add any missed context. otherwise I'll follow up post-shift with post-incident notes after infra and storage triage. :thumbsup:
Jordan (secondary): added a quick replay of the routing decision and config change in the incident doc. reference: https://confluence.redwood/ops/2026-03-15-embed-latency
incident-bot: update: monitor window started at 1769999860, p95 baseline 200ms, alert threshold 800ms.
Tony (ops): signing off — handover complete. @Priya @Jordan please ack when you have the runbook open and are watching dashboards.
Priya (primary): acked. watching grafana.
Jordan (secondary): ack. I'll take the first 30m watch then escalate if anything odd shows up.
